concepts.name: Ideal gas
concepts.statement: An ideal gas is made of particles that exert no forces on each other; they feel a force only when they collide, elastically, with the walls of the container.

concepts.name: Pressure
concepts.statement: The mechanical definition of pressure is the average force exerted on a wall divided by the wall's area.

concepts.name: Pressure from wall collisions
concepts.statement: A particle that bounces elastically between walls a distance a apart pushes on a wall with the force mv_x²/a; summed over N particles in a cubic box, the pressure is Nm⟨v_x²⟩/a³.

concepts.name: Mean square velocity component
concepts.statement: From the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution, the average of the square of a molecule's velocity along x is k_BT/m.

concepts.name: Ideal gas law
concepts.statement: The pressure, volume and temperature of an ideal gas are related by PV = Nk_BT = nRT, which per mole reads P V̄ = RT.

concepts.name: Equation of state
concepts.statement: An equation of state is a relation between the variables that describes the state of matter under a set of given physical conditions, such as the relation between P, V and T.

concepts.name: Isotherm
concepts.statement: An isotherm is a graph of P against V at a fixed temperature; for an ideal gas the isotherms are hyperbolas.

concepts.name: Isochore
concepts.statement: An isochore is a graph of P against T at a fixed volume; for an ideal gas it is a straight line whose slope grows with the density.

concepts.name: An ideal gas never condenses
concepts.statement: An ideal gas can exist only as a gas: it cannot condense into an ideal liquid, so a phase transition from gas to liquid can be modeled only if the interactions between particles are accounted for.

concepts.name: Compressibility factor
concepts.statement: The compressibility factor Z = PV/nRT is 1 for an ideal gas at every pressure, so for a real gas it measures how far the gas deviates from ideal behavior.

concepts.name: Dilute gases behave ideally
concepts.statement: At sufficiently low pressures, and so low densities, every real gas approaches ideal-gas behavior: its compressibility factor goes to 1.

concepts.name: System and surroundings
concepts.statement: Thermodynamics divides the universe into a system and its surroundings with a boundary between them; the three together are the thermodynamic universe.

concepts.name: Extensive and intensive properties
concepts.statement: If a system is grown with the ratio N/V held constant, a property that grows with it is extensive (N, n, V, m, energy) and one that stays the same is intensive (P, ρ, T, molar heat capacity).

concepts.name: Molar volume
concepts.statement: The molar volume V̄ = V/n is the volume per mole, an intensive quantity.

concepts.name: Density
concepts.statement: The density ρ = N/V is the number of particles per unit volume, an intensive quantity.

concepts.name: Van der Waals equation of state
terms: van der Waals equation of state
concepts.statement: The van der Waals equation adjusts the ideal gas law for the nonzero volume of the molecules, through b, and for the attraction between them, through a; with a and b zero it reduces to PV = nRT.

concepts.name: Hard-sphere potential
concepts.statement: The hard-wall potential treats molecules as billiard balls of diameter σ: no force acts until their centres are σ apart, and they can come no closer.

concepts.name: Hard-sphere diameter
concepts.statement: The diameter σ of a hard sphere is the distance between the centres of two spheres at closest contact.

concepts.name: Van der Waals constant b
concepts.statement: The constant b is the volume excluded by a mole of molecules: two hard spheres exclude a sphere of radius σ, 4πσ³/3, half of it to each, so b = (2/3)πσ³N₀ and n moles leave a volume V − nb free.

concepts.name: Attraction lowers the pressure
concepts.statement: The net force on the wall is the force of the impacts less the attraction of the other molecules, so a real gas presses less than an ideal one; the correction an²/V² grows with the square of the density.

concepts.name: Van der Waals constant a
concepts.statement: The constant a measures the attraction between the molecules of a substance; it lowers the pressure by an²/V². Like b, it depends on the substance.

concepts.name: Cubic equation of state
concepts.statement: Van der Waals-type equations of state are cubic: cubic polynomials in the molar volume and in the compressibility factor.

concepts.name: Redlich–Kwong equation of state
concepts.statement: Redlich and Kwong (1949) made the attraction term of van der Waals depend on temperature, as a/√T, and put the co-volume b into its denominator; the equation is generally more accurate than van der Waals above the critical temperature.

concepts.name: Redlich–Kwong cubic in Z
concepts.statement: With A = aP/R²T^2.5 and B = bP/RT, the Redlich–Kwong equation becomes a cubic in the compressibility factor.

concepts.name: Redlich–Kwong constants
concepts.statement: Imposing the criticality conditions on the Redlich–Kwong equation ties a and b to the critical temperature and pressure of the substance.

concepts.name: Redlich–Kwong equation in reduced variables
concepts.statement: Written in P_r and T_r, the Redlich–Kwong cubic holds the same for every gas: any two gases at the same reduced pressure and temperature have the same compressibility factor.

concepts.name: Mixing rules
concepts.statement: A cubic equation of state is applied to a mixture as to a pseudo pure substance whose a and b are averages of the components' over their mole fractions.

concepts.name: The van der Waals loop
concepts.statement: Below the critical temperature a van der Waals isotherm turns S-shaped, with a stretch where P and V increase together; there the curve is no longer physical.

concepts.name: Tie line
concepts.statement: In reality the pressure stays constant between the liquid and gas ends of the loop; the horizontal tie line represents gas–liquid coexistence, at the vapor pressure of the liquid.

concepts.name: Maxwell's construction
concepts.statement: The tie line is placed so that the area between it and the isotherm above the line equals the area below it.

concepts.name: Critical point
concepts.statement: On the critical isotherm the tie line shrinks to a single point, the critical point, where liquid and vapor become the same and the isotherm has an inflection.

concepts.name: Critical temperature
concepts.statement: The critical temperature T_c is the one temperature at which the critical point exists, the highest at which a gas–liquid transition can occur.

concepts.name: Supercritical fluid
concepts.statement: Above the critical temperature there is no liquid–gas transition; the fluid resembles a liquid at higher pressures and a gas at lower ones.

concepts.name: Criticality conditions
concepts.statement: At the critical point the first and second derivatives of P with respect to V vanish.

concepts.name: Critical volume
concepts.statement: The critical volume V_c is the volume at the critical point.

concepts.name: Critical pressure
concepts.statement: The critical pressure P_c is the pressure at the critical point.

concepts.name: Van der Waals critical constants
concepts.statement: The criticality conditions applied to the van der Waals equation give V_c = 3nb, RT_c = 8a/27b and P_c = a/27b².

concepts.name: Roots of a cubic equation of state
concepts.statement: A cubic equation of state has one real root above the critical temperature, three equal roots at the critical point, and three real roots below it only for pressures across the S-shaped loop; the smallest is the liquid's molar volume, the largest the vapor's, and the middle one has no physical meaning.

concepts.name: Gas–liquid coexistence region
concepts.statement: The curve through the ends of the tie lines peaks at the critical point; inside it gas and liquid coexist.

concepts.name: Compressibility chart
concepts.statement: Standing and Katz's chart (1942) plots measured compressibility factors against pressure; graphical reading of such charts was widespread until computers.

concepts.name: Reduced variables
concepts.statement: The reduced pressure, volume and temperature measure a substance's state against its own critical point: P_r = P/P_c, V_r = V/V_c, T_r = T/T_c.

concepts.name: Van der Waals equation in reduced variables
concepts.statement: In reduced variables the van der Waals equation takes one universal form, with no constant of the substance left in it.

concepts.name: Law of corresponding states
concepts.statement: Different gases at the same reduced temperature and reduced pressure behave alike: two gases are in corresponding states when their reduced pressure, volume and temperature are the same.

concepts.name: Critical compressibility of a van der Waals gas
concepts.statement: The van der Waals equation gives Z = 3/8 at the critical point, which does not agree well with measurement.

concepts.name: Compressibility factor in reduced variables
concepts.statement: The van der Waals compressibility factor is a universal function of the reduced volume and temperature.

concepts.name: Generalized compressibility chart
concepts.statement: Measured Z of different fluids plotted against reduced pressure fall on one set of curves; simple hydrocarbons, noble gases and diatomic molecules conform closely, while strongly polar or hydrogen-bonded fluids such as water, ammonia and HF deviate.

concepts.name: Virial equation of state
concepts.statement: The virial equation of state expresses the deviation from ideality as a power series in the density, with the second, third, … virial coefficients as the coefficients.

concepts.name: Intermolecular pair potential
concepts.statement: The intermolecular pair potential is the potential energy of two molecules as a function of their separation.

concepts.name: Mayer f-function
concepts.statement: The Mayer f-function, exp(−Φ₁₂/k_BT) − 1, is zero where the pair potential vanishes, −1 where it is infinitely repulsive and positive where it is attractive.

concepts.name: Configuration integral
concepts.statement: A configuration integral Z_j integrates the Boltzmann factor of the interaction energy of j molecules over all their positions; Z₁ = V.

concepts.name: Second virial coefficient
concepts.statement: The second virial coefficient gives the contribution of the pair potential to the pressure, the initial departure from ideal-gas behavior; it is an integral of the Mayer f-function over the separation.

forms.latex: B_{2}= \dfrac{1}{2} \iint v_{\mathrm {excluded}} (\Omega,\Omega') f(\Omega) f(\Omega')~ {\mathrm d}\Omega {\mathrm d}\Omega'

concepts.name: Second virial coefficient of hard spheres
concepts.statement: For hard spheres of diameter σ, B₂ = 2πσ³/3, independent of temperature.

concepts.name: Isihara–Hadwiger formula
concepts.statement: For any hard convex body, B₂ = RS + V exactly, where V is its volume, S its surface area and R its mean radius of curvature.

concepts.name: Second virial coefficient of a van der Waals gas
concepts.statement: For the van der Waals equation of state, B₂ = b − a/RT: the excluded volume raises it and the attraction lowers it, more so the colder the gas.

concepts.name: Lennard-Jones potential
concepts.statement: The Lennard-Jones potential describes the potential energy of two nonbonding atoms or molecules against their separation: a steep r⁻¹² repulsive term and a smoother r⁻⁶ attractive term.

concepts.name: Lennard-Jones σ
concepts.statement: σ is the separation at which the Lennard-Jones potential is zero, a measure of how close two nonbonding particles can get.

concepts.name: Van der Waals radius
concepts.statement: The van der Waals radius is one-half of the internuclear distance between nonbonding particles, σ/2.

concepts.name: Kinds of intermolecular attraction
concepts.statement: Neutral molecules attract one another through dipole–dipole, dipole–induced dipole and London (dispersion) interactions.

concepts.name: Repulsion and attraction in the Lennard-Jones potential
concepts.statement: Far apart, two particles barely interact; brought closer they attract and become bound, down to an equilibrium separation; pressed closer still, their electrons are forced into each other's orbitals and the repulsion soars.

concepts.name: Forces along the Lennard-Jones curve
concepts.statement: A particle feels a repulsive force closer than the equilibrium distance r_min, an attractive force beyond it and no force at it, slightly beyond σ, where the potential is at its minimum and the pair is most stable.

concepts.name: Evaluating the Lennard-Jones potential
concepts.statement: Given ε, σ and a separation r, substitute into V(r) = 4ε[(σ/r)¹² − (σ/r)⁶] to find the intermolecular potential, and read off from σ whether it should be positive or negative.

concepts.name: Virial expansion of the van der Waals equation
concepts.statement: Expanding 1/(1 − b/V̄) as a series turns the van der Waals equation into a virial series whose second coefficient is b − a/RT.

concepts.name: Dispersion coefficient C₆
concepts.statement: C₆ is the strength of the intermolecular attraction that falls off as r⁻⁶.

concepts.name: Hard sphere with an r⁻⁶ attraction
concepts.statement: Combining the hard sphere with the attractive part of the Lennard-Jones potential gives an infinite wall at σ and −C₆/r⁶ beyond it.

concepts.name: Van der Waals constants from molecular parameters
concepts.statement: For hard spheres with an r⁻⁶ attraction, B₂ takes the van der Waals form b − a/RT with b = (2/3)πN₀σ³, four times the volume of the molecules, and a proportional to C₆: van der Waals assumes hard spheres at small distances and weak attractions at larger ones.
